properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4115001, 4115003 and 4115004 (recorded 2019-02-07, mapped 2019-03-14, active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): a fresh programmatic color-trace (RGB [128,193,219]) matched this block's old area closely (~75800 vs ~75400 px2) but only ~44% by IoU -- the old shape was a similar size but shifted/rotated relative to the true diagram fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color and extracted its precise 7-vertex contour (OpenCV), capturing the block's real angled SW corner near the PG&E switchyard. Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with HDY1/2 or H1. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (found via join_approximate.py's new MAJOR CLIP warning, prompted by user-flagged issues elsewhere): confirmed via direct satellite comparison that this block's west/SW portion sits on a real, currently-paved curving driveway near the PG&E switchyard (visible pavement with a clear curb), not vacant land -- 34% of this block's area was inside the buffered real-street layer. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer, same pattern already used for Parcels D/E1/H1/H2/E4; area dropped from ~7,260 to ~4,815 sq m. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'F/G can expand a beat east to Louisiana like its northern neighbors'): this block's own north-facing boundary (the notch left by the driveway clip above) dipped 6-45m west of the Louisiana St offset line that C1/C2 now front (9.8m west of the real centerline) -- a real, if modest by area, discrepancy against the '...like its northern neighbors' standard. Pushed the notch's own vertices (the ones between the SW switchyard corner, left untouched since that's a distinct, separately-confirmed real driveway curve, and the point already east of the line near C1/C2) out to the Louisiana offset line at each vertex's own latitude; several of the resulting points landed within a meter of each other (since the pushed edge is now close to straight) and were simplified away (shapely simplify, ~0.05m tolerance) rather than left as a stack of near-duplicate vertices. Confirmed 0 overlap with C1 and C2. Area drops from ~4,815 to ~3,548 sq m, despite this being an eastward 'expansion' -- the removed notch was a westward bulge (the driveway-clip trace curving further west than the Louisiana line, not a dent cutting into the block), so pulling that curve back east to a straight, Louisiana-aligned edge nets less area even though the edge itself moved toward the target frontage. Visually, this reads as the north edge now sitting flush with C1/C2's own Louisiana frontage instead of bulging west of it. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the DataSF identifiers named above (Building 14's footprint under blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel blklot 4114010) are our own lookups in DataSF's Building Footprints and Assessor parcels layers, not statements in the D4D, which this file cites only for the diagram. Assessor lot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF acdm-wktn) and its legacy id is carried by 21 building footprints, so the id does not by itself identify Building 14; 4114010 is an active P70-MU lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name as Building 12. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this file uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner said F/G should extend west and follow the road curve, and asked whether the parcel had an Assessor lot. Checking DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) found three active lots in block 4115 -- 4115003 (3,792 m2), 4115001 (a 647 m2 sliver) and 4115004 (3,235 m2), all mapped 2019-03-14 -- whose union is a single 7,674 m2 polygon with the same pointed west tip and slanted south-west edge along the curving road that D4D Figure 6.4.2 draws for F/G (the figure's raw trace measured about 7,260 m2). The outline is now that union, using the lots' own vertices (89 vertices, no simplification), in place of the traced 8-vertex shape of about 3,539 m2 that had been clipped against the real-street corridor and pulled east to Louisiana St. It overlaps no other Pier 70 shape. The identification of these lots as F/G is an inference from location, shape and area only; no Port document read names them, which supersedes the earlier statement above that the lot had not been checked at all. geometry_type is now 'real' because the edges are recorded lot lines. 2026-10-11: text only. Measured the lot union against the street corridor (src/street_geometry.py, DataSF official centerlines, 6.8 m half-width plus surveyed curbs): about 21% of its area lies inside the corridor and a further 2% is cut off from the main piece by it; the build (join_approximate.py) reports 24% removed. accuracy_caveat now says so. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of three real Assessor lots (4115001, 4115003 and 4115004), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That these three lots are Parcels F/G is Pier & Point's own inference from their location, shape and size (7,674 m2, against about 7,260 m2 measured on D4D Figure 6.4.2; both show the same pointed west tip and slanted south-west edge along the curving road). No Port document read ties these lot numbers to F/G. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). Along the curving south road, the map clips about 24% of the lot union as street: about 21% (roughly 1,650 m2 of 7,690 m2) falls inside the street corridor drawn from DataSF's official centerlines (6.8 m each side), and about 2% more is cut off from the rest by that corridor and dropped. The outline shown is therefore smaller than the three lots together.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot matches F/G. Three adjacent active lots in block 4115 (4115001, 4115003 and 4115004) together cover it, so its shape is their union rather than one status.csv row; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
properties.regulatory_context: Flexible use: the D4D's Figure 2.1.1 stripes F/G Commercial-Office and Residential (commercial in the Mid-Point baseline scenario; 'life science' does not appear in the D4D for F/G), shown as ONE combined parcel 'F/G' in the D4D's own Figure 6.4.2 (not two separate parcels 'F' and 'G'), 90 ft max, and per D4D Section 6.4.2 commercial buildings are limited to six stories (a residential building may have nine), so the six-story figure holds only if F/G is built as commercial. It is in subphase 2A of the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan (Port Item 11A, Exhibit A). A '+/- 410,000 RSF' figure previously recorded here came from an uncited leasing brochure and has been dropped. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Parcels F/G of the Pier 70 Design for Development, shown as the union of Assessor lots 4115001, 4115003 and 4115004 (see the accuracy note). Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026), which says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward.
